limits: a neighbour on a class section 5 does not price contributes nothing -- 89 of the board's GND pads have no priced neighbour and fall to the floor

the MAXIMUM neighbour is charged, not the sum, which under-charges a multi-rail part; it sits against a much larger over-charge in the other direction, since each rail is charged WHOLE to one ground pad that draws a fraction of it

question: PP2 refused EVERY split of the board's return pour with NET_CARRIES_NO_PUBLISHED_CURRENT, because .kicad_dru section 5 prices nine RAILS and none of them is GND.  What does a return fragment actually have to carry?

rejected.bar: the strictest figure section 5 publishes anywhere (BAT_MAIN 3.125 A)
rejected.why: it is not the analogue of what D-628 did.  D-628 charges a +3V3 fragment the WHOLE +3V3 rail because every pad on it is a pad OF that rail; the whole-NET analogue for a return net is the sum of every rail on the board (~9.3 A), which no 1 oz outer fragment could meet -- so it is the unconditional refusal again wearing a number.  And 3.125 A REFUSES the C45/C51/C53 pocket at 2.552 A, the very fragment this contract's own doctrine defends in prose as 'not a return-path injury; it is what those barrels are for'.
